messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: want gradient from rstan
parts:
Hi, I fit a Stan model and now I want the gradient as a function of the parameters in the original space (I think that's what's called the constrained parameters in the rstan documentation).

Suppose I have a stanfit object called "fit" and 3000 simulation draws (which I can get using extract(fit)). I want the gradient for each of these simulation draws. I'm confused trying to figure out how to do this using grad_log_prob. It seems like I have to extract the simulations, pull them out one at a time, then put them back into lists. There must be an easier way, no?

Also it seems that grad_log_prob gives me the gradient on the unconstrained space. How to I get the gradients on the original (constrained) space?

Thx
A

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: want gradient from rstan
parts:
On Wednesday, December 7, 2016 at 9:49:23 PM UTC-5, Andrew Gelman wrote:
Suppose I have a stanfit object called "fit" and 3000 simulation draws (which I can get using extract(fit)).  I want the gradient for each of these simulation draws.  I'm confused trying to figure out how to do this using grad_log_prob.  It seems like I have to extract the simulations, pull them out one at a time, then put them back into lists.  There must be an easier way, no?
No, due to the fact that the compiled Stan function can only input a vector of (unconstrained) parameters.
Also it seems that grad_log_prob gives me the gradient on the unconstrained space.  How to I get the gradients on the original (constrained) space?

There is an adjust_transform argument that is TRUE by default which indicates that the gradient calculation should be with respect to the constrained parameters. So, all together it would be

pars <- as.matrix(posterior)
skel <- get_inits(posterior)[[1]]
grad <- t(apply(pars, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(theta) {
  grad_log_prob(posterior, upars = unconstrain_pars(posterior, relist(theta, skel)))
}))
colnames(grad) <- colnames(pars)

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] want gradient from rstan
parts:
No, I don't think you can get the derivative with respect to the parameter on the constrained space.  adjust_transform is used only for whether the Jacobian adjustment is done or not for the log-posterior.  (Ben, right?)

Jiqiang

parts: If you needed it, we can get that in C++ without much effort, I think. We can devise some way to get that out. grad_log_prob() wasn't designed for that purpose, so it wouldn't be appropriate to retrofit it for that functionality. It's really a matter of specifying what you want out from some input.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] want gradient from rstan
parts:
We've just had this discussion on the dev list:

http://discourse.mc-stan.org/t/feature-request-jacobians-of-unconstraining-transform/154/1

and I believe Ryan was suggesting what Ben was suggesting
and I said the same thing as Jiqiang.

I don't think this can be fished out of a current compiled
model. It would be possible to generate just the constrained
function call. In fact, we could factor the code generation
that way, which we've also been talking about. But we need to
get rid of the derivative w.r.t. the transform as well as
the Jacobian calcs.

- Bob
